THORChain spans 13 chains. For Ethereum: 10 addresses catalogued (see D1). For Bitcoin, BCH, Doge, LTC, Ripple, Cosmos, Tron, Solana, Avalanche, Binance, Base: THORChain uses dynamically rotating Asgard vault addresses on each native chain (not fixed EVM contracts) that change with each 'churn' cycle. The ETH Router contract (0xD37BbE5744D730a1d98d8DC97c42F0Ca46aD7146) is not a factory; it manages vault allowances and routes deposits to dynamic Asgard vault addresses. The Asgard vault addresses on Ethereum (0x6c76e20C..., 0xa5749368..., 0xA772Bdd2..., 0x2951Cc0F..., 0x330c8eE5...) are EOAs funded by the router representing the current/historical Asgard TSS vaults. protocol_metadata.about: THORChain is a decentralized cross-chain liquidity protocol built as a Cosmos-based layer-1 blockchain that enables users to swap native assets (BTC, ETH, SOL, etc.) across 14 blockchains directly from self-custody wallets without wrapped tokens or bridges. Users send native assets to dynamically rotating Asgard vault addresses (controlled by a threshold-signature-scheme node network) on each supported chain, with the THORChain L1 network observing inbound transactions and executing swaps. Liquidity providers deposit paired assets into RUNE-denominated pools, where RUNE serves as the universal settlement asset and is bonded by nodes as economic security. The protocol charges liquidity fees paid in RUNE and distributes yield to liquidity providers and node operators.
